headline: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, boosting AI agentic workloads.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open model designed for high-volume agentic workloads, is now accessible via Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. This model features a 30 billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts architecture, with 3 billion active parameters, promising up to 4x higher throughput and 30% faster task completion rates. The integration into SageMaker allows developers to deploy this model efficiently for various AI applications. This advancement highlights NVIDIA's commitment to enhancing AI model performance and accessibility.
items.why_it_matters: This release is crucial for tech leads focusing on AI tools development, providing a scalable, high-performance model option that integrates seamlessly into existing AWS workflows.

items.title: Build OpenClaw agents that transact with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
items.summary: AWS introduces a new integration allowing autonomous agents to make transactions using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments. The system leverages the aws-agents-pay plugin to facilitate controlled spending on paywalled APIs and MCP servers, ensuring transactions are bounded and human-approved. This setup enhances agent autonomy while maintaining financial oversight.

items.title: Developing Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 with QAD Using NVIDIA Model Optimizer
items.summary: NVIDIA introduces optimizations for the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 model, utilizing the NVIDIA Model Optimizer and QAD techniques. These optimizations aim to enhance model performance by refining parameters and reducing computational overhead, making it more suitable for deployment on diverse hardware configurations.

items.title: The Unwritten Benchmark: A New Challenge for Multimodal Machine Learning in Abstract Perceptual Reasoning
items.summary: A new arXiv paper introduces 'The Unwritten Benchmark', focusing on the capacity of multimodal models to perform abstract perceptual reasoning, which involves inferring unseen information from dynamic processes. This benchmark aims to evaluate the ability of models to go beyond static content recognition.

items.title: Toward Safe LLM Agents: A Survey of Specification, Verification, and Enforcement
items.summary: This survey paper on arXiv addresses the safety challenges of LLM agents performing irreversible actions. It examines current approaches to ensure task-level safety through specification, verification, and enforcement, crucial for AI systems that interact with real-world environments.
